articles.title: Peão goiano está entre os 20 mais bem pagos em montarias nos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Atualmente, o atleta integra o time Arizona Ridge Riders nas competições dos EUA. Além dele, outros 19 atletas brasileiros integram a lista que conta com 50 nomes.
articles.summary: Atleta de montaria de touros integra o time Arizona Ridge Riders nas competições dos EUA. Além dele, outros 19 atletas brasileiros integram a lista que conta com 50 nomes.
articles.body:
Um peão goiano está na 15ª posição da lista de atletas mais bem pagos de montaria em touros dos Estados Unidos, reunida pela Professional Bull Riders (PBR). O espaço foi ocupado por Eduardo Aparecido, de 36 anos, de Gouvelândia , na região sudoeste de Goiás, com o valor acumulado durante a carreira de US$ 3,03 milhões (cerca de R$ 15,2 milhões na cotação atual).

A PBR é a maior organização e liga internacional do esporte, e realiza eventos de montaria nos Estados Unidos, Brasil e outros países. De acordo com informações da organização, Eduardo foi campeão brasileiro e duas vezes campeão global da PBR.

De acordo com a biografia do atleta no site da liga, Eduardo, conhecido como "Fast Eddy", aprendeu a montar enquanto trabalhava em um rancho em Gouvelândia e, com 18 anos, começou a competir profissionalmente. Em 2016, ele atingiu a pontuação suficiente para se tornar o campeão brasileiro da PBR e conquistou a primeira oportunidade de chegar as finais no torneio internacional.

Desde então, Eduardo se classificou para 13 finais. Sua maior pontuação no esporte era de 96.1 até a última atualização desta reportagem.

O sistema de pontuações no esporte pode chegar ao número máximo de 100, com os pontos sendo distribuídos entre animal e montador — 50 para cada. Para conquistar a maior marca, os juízes observam não somente o tempo de 8 segundos que o peão consegue permanecer montado no animal, mas também equilíbrio do atleta e a força dos pulos e coices do touro.

Além de Eduardo, outros brasileiros ocupam a lista, inclusive o primeiro lugar. Entre os 50 primeiros nomes do ranking, 19 são brasileiros.

Atualmente, Eduardo integra o time Arizona Ridge Riders e continua participando de competições nos Estados Unidos.

articles.title: Assédio eleitoral na Bahia: MPT processa rede de supermercados | G1
articles.standfirst: Órgão afirma que funcionários eram obrigados a usar camisas com número igual ao de um candidato. Empresa teria mantido prática mesmo após recomendação para interrompê-la.
articles.summary: O MPT processa a Rede Mix por assédio eleitoral na Bahia após denúncias de que funcionários eram obrigados a usar camisas com o número de um candidato.
articles.body:
MPT processa rede varejista por suspeita de assédio eleitoral contra trabalhadores na Bahia — Foto: Divulgação

O Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT) entrou com uma ação na Justiça contra a empresa varejista Rede Mix, nesta sexta-feira (23), por suspeita de assédio eleitoral contra trabalhadores na Bahia.

O órgão afirma que funcionários eram obrigados a usar uniformes com um número igual ao de um dos candidatos que disputam o segundo turno das eleições de 2026.

O MPT pediu uma decisão liminar para suspender imediatamente o uso das camisas ligadas à campanha de aniversário da rede de supermercados. O órgão considera que a iniciativa pode constranger os empregados e interferir na liberdade de escolha política e no direito ao voto.

Segundo a procuradora do Trabalho Manuella Gedeon, responsável pela ação, o caso começou a ser investigado após denúncias de que funcionários eram obrigados a vestir as camisas durante o expediente.

Por meio de nota, a RedeMix informou que número presente nas camisetas utilizadas por seus colaboradores faz referência exclusivamente ao aniversário da empresa, celebrados em 2026. (Confira nota na íntegra ao final da matéria)

Em outro comunicado, a empresa disse que atendeu à solicitação do Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT), apresentando a documentação referente às campanhas institucionais de aniversário realizadas em anos anteriores.

De acordo com o MPT, o órgão também recebeu fotografias que mostrariam trabalhadores usando as peças diante de colegas, clientes e outras pessoas.

Após receber as primeiras denúncias, o MPT enviou uma recomendação à Rede Mix para que interrompesse qualquer prática que pudesse configurar assédio eleitoral e revisasse campanhas promocionais com referências que pudessem ser interpretadas como mensagens políticas.

Segundo o órgão, a recomendação foi entregue pessoalmente à empresa. Mesmo assim, novas denúncias apontaram que os funcionários continuavam usando os uniformes.

O MPT afirma ainda que uma fiscalização realizada por servidores da área de segurança institucional constatou a continuidade do uso das camisas com o numeral.

Além da suspensão imediata do uso das camisas, o Ministério Público do Trabalho quer que a Rede Mix substitua os uniformes por roupas neutras até o fim do processo eleitoral.

O órgão também pede que a empresa divulgue um comunicado interno para garantir aos funcionários a liberdade de orientação política e o direito ao voto livre e secreto. Outro pedido é a aplicação de multa diária de pelo menos R$ 50 mil para cada obrigação descumprida.

O MPT solicita ainda que a empresa adote medidas para garantir que os trabalhadores escalados para trabalhar no dia da votação tenham tempo suficiente para votar.

O órgão pretende apresentar posteriormente uma ação civil pública para discutir o caso e pedir eventual indenização por danos morais coletivos, caso as irregularidades sejam confirmadas.

A ação apresentada nesta sexta-feira é cautelar e busca medidas imediatas para interromper a prática apontada pelo MPT. A suspeita de assédio eleitoral ainda será analisada pela Justiça do Trabalho.

"A RedeMiX esclarece que o número presente nas camisetas utilizadas por seus colaboradores faz referência exclusivamente ao aniversário da RedeMiX, celebrados em 2026.

A identificação integra a campanha institucional de aniversário da rede, realizada anualmente entre final de setembro a novembro, seguindo uma prática de comunicação alinhada à identidade da marca. Uma celebração que reúne clientes, colaboradores e parceiros em torno de uma trajetória construída com dedicação, confiança e vínculos com a comunidade."

"A RedeMix informa que atendeu à solicitação do Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT), apresentando a documentação referente às campanhas institucionais de aniversário realizadas em anos anteriores, que demonstram a continuidade dessa prática de comunicação da empresa.

Sobre o processo citado na reportagem, ainda não fomos notificados e por isso não temos conhecimento do teor da ação.

A rede permanece à disposição do órgão para prestar os esclarecimentos necessários e reafirma as informações já divulgadas em sua nota oficial."

articles.title: Seca: Governo de MG decreta situação de emergência em cidades do Norte de MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Mais de 80 das 105 cidades estão localizadas no Norte de Minas Gerais. A medida foi publicada no Decreto nº 1.039, de 23 de outubro de 2026, e tem validade de 180 dias.
articles.summary: Mais de 80 das 105 cidades estão localizadas no Norte de Minas Gerais.
articles.body:
O Governo de Minas Gerais decretou situação de emergência em mais de municípios devido aos impactos provocados pela seca. Mais de 80 das 105 cidades estão localizadas no Norte de Minas Gerais. A medida foi publicada no Decreto nº 1.039, no Diário Oficial desta sexta-feira (23), e tem validade de 180 dias.

Segundo o governo estadual, a decisão foi tomada em razão da diminuição ou do esgotamento das reservas hídricas que abastecem os municípios atingidos. O decreto destaca que várias cidades já enfrentam problemas no fornecimento de água para a população.

Local onde o rio Mocambo passava em Coração de Jesus — Foto: Inter TV/Reprodução

O documento também considera a necessidade de atuação conjunta dos integrantes do Sistema Nacional de Proteção e Defesa Civil para minimizar os efeitos do desastre.

Conforme o texto, a interrupção das ações de resposta à seca, por meio da operação de Transporte e Distribuição de Água Potável (TDAP), pode causar prejuízos aos municípios afetados.

Com o decreto, fica autorizada a mobilização dos órgãos de defesa civil para prestar apoio complementar às cidades atingidas, sob coordenação do Gabinete Militar do Governador e da Coordenadoria Estadual de Defesa Civil de Minas Gerais.

Falta de chuvas muda paisagem no Norte de MG e adeta vida de produtores rurais — Foto: Inter TV/Reprodução

Entre as ações previstas estão o fornecimento de kits de ajuda humanitária, reservatórios de água e a prestação de serviços de transporte e distribuição de água potável. O atendimento deverá seguir critérios técnicos definidos pela Defesa Civil.

De acordo com o decreto, a situação de emergência é válida apenas para as áreas comprovadamente afetadas pela seca e registradas pelos municípios no Sistema Integrado de Informações sobre Desastres (S2ID).

articles.title: BYD quer dobrar capacidade de produção | G1
articles.standfirst: A marca prometeu nacionalizar, até 2027, mais de 50% da produção de peças, incluindo processos de estamparia, pintura e soldagem de componentes dos veículos.
articles.summary: A marca prometeu nacionalizar, até 2027, mais de 50% da produção de peças, incluindo processos de estamparia, pintura e soldagem de componentes dos veículos
articles.body:
Fábrica da BYD em Camaçari (BA) — Foto: divulgação/BYD

A fabricante chinesa de carros elétricos BYD iniciou os pedidos de licenças para dobrar para 600.000 veículos a capacidade anual de produção de sua fábrica brasileira. Ao mesmo tempo, a empresa entra na fase final de obras e testes dos galpões de estamparia, soldagem e pintura, disse à Reuters o principal executivo da companhia no país.

A unidade da BYD no Brasil deve iniciar 2027 com mais do que o mínimo exigido de 50% de nacionalização de componentes. Isso permitirá à empresa atender às exigências regulatórias e iniciar as exportações regionais, afirmou em entrevista o vice-presidente sênior Alexandre Baldy.

A empresa enfrentou reclamações de grupos da indústria local por depender muito de importações e de tarifas temporariamente baixas.

"A gente trabalha para inaugurar 2027 já ultrapassando essa posição e termos essas etapas em operação para sermos considerados um fabricante local", disse Baldy.

A BYD tem como meta se tornar a maior montadora do Brasil em volume de vendas até 2030, mas a demanda já supera sua capacidade atual de produção, disse Baldy. Veja ranking de produção de automóveis e comerciais leves:

RENAULT GEELY DO BRASIL : 184.914 unidades

* Dados de produção da Associação Nacional dos Fabricantes de Veículos Automotores (Anfavea)

Embora esteja acelerando suas operações e planeje atingir uma produção mensal de 25.000 veículos até o fim de 2026, a BYD prevê que a demanda continuará superando a oferta.

"Nossa demanda tem ficado em uma média de cerca de 30.000 carros por mês, o que significa que estamos deixando de faturar cerca de 5.000 a 6.000 vendas adicionais", disse Baldy.

O investimento na nova fábrica da empresa no Brasil já ultrapassou R$ 5,5 bilhões, e as vendas faturadas da unidade brasileira atingirão nesta semana a marca de 200.000 carros no acumulado de 2026, afirmou Baldy.

Em setembro, a empresa teve 22.209 veículos emplacados no Brasil, o equivalente a uma fatia de 8,5% do mercado, segundo dados da companhia.

A BYD já é líder de mercado no Uruguai e ocupa posições de destaque em vendas na Colômbia e na Argentina, disse o executivo.

A montadora no Brasil também recebeu pedidos de 50.000 unidades do México e outras 50.000 da Argentina. A empresa estará apta a atendê-los a partir do ano que vem graças ao aumento do índice de componentes locais.

A BYD inaugurou sua fábrica em Camaçari, na Bahia, em 9 de outubro de 2025, em um complexo industrial que pertenceu à Ford.

A fábrica emprega atualmente cerca de 9.000 pessoas e espera ampliar esse número para cerca de 10.000 até o fim deste ano.

articles.title: Caminhão invade casa e destrói quarto de criança de 10 anos em Biritiba Mirim | G1
articles.standfirst: Moradores afirmam que já haviam alertado a Prefeitura sobre os riscos da circulação de veículos pesados na rua. Ninguém ficou ferido.
articles.summary: Moradores afirmam que já haviam alertado a Prefeitura sobre os riscos da circulação de veículos pesados na rua. Ninguém ficou ferido.
articles.body:
Um caminhão atingiu uma casa e derrubou parte da parede do quarto de uma criança de 10 anos, na manhã desta sexta-feira (23), em Biritiba Mirim. Ninguém ficou ferido. Segundo os moradores, outros casos envolvendo caminhões já haviam sido registrados no mesmo local.

O acidente aconteceu por volta das 7h15, na avenida Benedito de Miranda Melo, no bairro Vertentes. A médica Danysa Nascimento, mãe do menino, contou à TV Diário que estava se arrumando para trabalhar quando ouviu um estrondo. Ela e o marido correram até o quarto do filho.

"Entramos correndo no quarto do meu filho e, graças a Deus, a cama está intacta, mas tudo ao redor caiu. O banheiro caiu", relatou.

Segundo a médica, a família já havia alertado a Prefeitura sobre os riscos da circulação de caminhões que transportam materiais de uma pedreira da região. Ela afirma que protocolou uma reclamação no dia 2 de outubro, mas que o pedido ainda está em análise.

"Há meses, há anos, o bairro inteiro fala sobre os riscos que a gente está correndo. Eu acredito que seja sobrepeso dos caminhões da pedreira", afirmou.

Danysa também relatou que os veículos enfrentam dificuldades para subir a rua e, frequentemente, precisam dar marcha à ré ou fazer manobras para conseguir passar.

Caminhão bateu em muro e destruiu interior de casa em Biritiba Mirim — Foto: Danysa Nascimento/Arquivo Pessoal

"Toda manhã, a partir das 5h30, é o barulho deles tentando voltar para pegar mais impulso para conseguir subir."

O marido dela, o mestre de capoeira Oriel Rezende, afirmou que esta é a terceira ou quarta vez que um caminhão se envolve em um acidente em frente à residência.

Segundo ele, em uma das ocorrências, um veículo desceu de ré e quase atingiu um poste e o muro da casa. Em outra, o motorista precisou descarregar parte do pó de pedra transportado para conseguir retirar o caminhão.

"Semana passada, esse caminhão também desceu, entrou na minha garagem. Nós fizemos vídeos, entramos em contato também, e foi a mesma coisa", contou.

Após o acidente desta sexta-feira, o caminhão foi retirado com a ajuda de um trator da Prefeitura.

A família também acionou a polícia e solicitou uma avaliação das condições do imóvel. Segundo Danysa, há rachaduras em outras paredes da residência, e os moradores aguardam uma análise técnica para saber se poderão continuar na casa.

Em nota, a Prefeitura de Biritiba Mirim informou que acompanha a ocorrência desde as 7h, quando tomou conhecimento do caso, e que mobilizou uma equipe de trânsito para atuar no local.

A administração municipal destacou que a pedreira é uma empresa privada e que deverá responder pelos danos relacionados à atividade, caso sejam constatadas responsabilidades.

A Prefeitura também esclareceu que a circulação de caminhões pela rota utilizada é permitida pelo Decreto Municipal nº 3.644, de 1º de dezembro de 2021. Segundo a administração, existem normas que restringem o uso da área central como acesso à rodovia e que devem ser cumpridas pela empresa.

Ainda de acordo com a Prefeitura, as circunstâncias do acidente serão apuradas pelos órgãos competentes. Um laudo pericial deverá ajudar a identificar as responsabilidades e definir as medidas legais cabíveis.

A administração municipal afirmou que está prestando assistência à família e acompanhando as avaliações técnicas necessárias.

articles.title: Mostra de cinema em Maceió exibe curtas de terror no Halloween | G1
articles.standfirst: Sessão especial acontece nesta sexta-feira (23), às 18h, na Casa Sambacaitá, e reúne produções de terror, suspense e fantasia dirigidas por cineastas do estado.
articles.summary: A Mostra de cinema em Maceió apresenta oito curtas de realizadores locais na Casa Sambacaitá nesta sexta-feira (23), com entrada franca e foco no gênero de terror.
articles.body:
O terror, o suspense e a fantasia produzidos em Alagoas ganham espaço em uma sessão gratuita especial de Halloween nesta sexta-feira (23), em Maceió . A Mostra Filé de Cinema reúne oito curtas-metragens de realizadores alagoanos, a partir das 18h, na Casa Sambacaitá, com histórias que exploram desde o sobrenatural até os medos e conflitos do cotidiano.

A programação destaca a diversidade do cinema independente produzido no estado e busca ampliar as oportunidades de exibição para cineastas locais. Os filmes percorrem diferentes caminhos narrativos, com tramas que envolvem desaparecimentos, acontecimentos inexplicáveis, memórias, luto e sobrevivência.

Entre os destaques está Santo Errado (2025), dirigido por Daniel Ricardo. O curta acompanha Ezequiel em uma tentativa de invocar um amor na sexta-feira 13, dia de Santo Antônio. A história ganha continuidade em Uma Suíte Sobre o Caso Santo Errado (2026), também dirigida por Ricardo, em que quatro estudantes investigam um desaparecimento no Pontal da Barra e acabam envolvidos em um pesadelo.

A sessão também apresenta As Câmeras do Edifício Palmer, de Otávio Santana, sobre acontecimentos estranhos em um prédio residencial; Minha Única Amiga, de Mariah Medeiros, que acompanha um garoto introvertido durante uma noite caótica; e Viagem Perdida, de Clara Macedo, que explora as memórias, os medos e os sonhos de duas amigas em um reencontro marcado por situações difíceis de explicar.

Outras produções ampliam o olhar da mostra sobre as possibilidades do cinema de gênero. Em Onde Mora o Medo, Lucas Pillar entrelaça histórias, causos e tradições em uma narrativa que transita entre realidade e imaginário.

Já Rota de Fuga, de Henrique Oliveira e Ricardo Oliveira, aborda pertencimento, luto e memória em um bairro ameaçado de desaparecer após décadas de exploração mineral. Com direção coletiva, Três Quarteirões transforma o trajeto cotidiano de uma jovem em uma jornada de proteção e sobrevivência.

A sessão especial dá continuidade ao trabalho da Mostra Filé de Cinema de ampliar a circulação de filmes de ficção produzidos em Alagoas. A primeira edição do evento ocorreu nos dias 21 e 22 de março de 2026, também na Casa Sambacaitá, e reuniu 19 curtas-metragens de realizadores do estado em sessões competitivas e paralelas.

Nesta edição temática, a iniciativa dedica a programação ao cinema de gênero e evidencia a variedade de histórias, estilos e abordagens presentes na produção audiovisual independente alagoana.

A Mostra Filé de Cinema é uma iniciativa independente idealizada pela Daniel Ricardo Filmes, voltada à valorização e à difusão do cinema de ficção produzido em Alagoas. A edição especial conta com o apoio da Casa Sambacaitá, da Secretaria Municipal da Mulher, Pessoas com Deficiência, Idosos e Cidadania (SEMUC) e do Porto Sol Maceió.

articles.title: 'Se não tem no Google, tem no Alecrim': bairro em Natal faz 115 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo dados da AEBA, mais de 100 mil pessoas circulam por dia no bairro, um dos centros comerciais mais importantes da capital potiguar. Trabalhadores cobram melhorias.
articles.summary: Segundo dados da AEBA, mais de 100 mil pessoas circulam por dia no bairro, um dos centros comerciais mais importantes da capital potiguar. Trabalhadores cobram melhorias.
articles.body:
Jani, Ronaldo e Maria Luiza trabalham no Alecrim — Foto: Victor Eduardo/Inter TV

"Se não tem no Google, tem no Alecrim" . Essa afirmação virou um lema do bairro Alecrim, na Zona Leste de Natal , nos últimos anos. A frase reitera a variedade de produtos no bairro - um dos principais centros comerciais da capital potiguar - mesmo em meio à era digital e de vendas on-line.

Nesta sexta-feira (23), o Alecrim completa 115 anos e mantém a fama de ter todo e qualquer produto que o cliente procura. E os trabalhadores do bairro garantem que isso é verdade.

"No Alecrim tudo tem, viu? O que você não encontrar no Google, uma frase certa que já foi dita, você encontra aqui no Alecrim", garante a comerciante Jani Rocha, que há 25 anos trabalha no bairro.

"É assim mesmo, verdadeiramente é assim. Você chega hoje atrás de um produto, aí eu digo para o meu fornecedor que está tendo muita procura disso e, de imediato, já se fabrica e já chega"".

📊 Segundo dados da Associação dos Empresários do Bairro Alecrim (AEBA) divulgados em junho deste ano, o Alecrim conta com 6.055 empresas ativas , tendo aumentado mais de 10% ao ano desde 2022.

📊 A estimativa da AEBA é que mais de 100 mil pessoas circulem diariamente pelas ruas do bairro, sendo mais de 3 milhões por mês.

O bairro conta com shoppings, supermercados, mercado público, bancos, cartórios, órgãos públicos e lojas de diversos segmentos - algumas com décadas de funcionamento. E um dos principais atrativos comerciais é o camelódromo.

Jani Rocha, que trabalha como camelô no bairro há 25 anos, diz que o trabalho e o bairro foram responsáveis por lhe garantir o sustento e diversas amizades cultivadas ao longo dos anos.

"Eu digo que o Alecrim é minha casa, é o meu lar. Transformei o Alecrim no meu lar, por isso que eu cuido", disse.

➡️ Há um projeto de revitalização do camelódromo - que já chegou a ser discutido em audiência pública - que ainda não saiu do papel.

O comerciante Ronaldo Tavares, de 70 anos, conta que chegou ao Alecrim aos 8 anos de idade e há mais de cinco décadas trabalha no bairro.

Ele recorda como o bairro foi tomando o aspecto de centro comercial importante da capital potiguar ao longo dos anos. Onde ele morava, conta, eram poucas casas e nada de asfalto.

"Eram casas de taipa, vilas. Tinham 23 casas, 12 de um lado e 11 do outro. E a gente jogava bola aqui, era só areia. Loja praticamente não tinha nada", contou.

Ronaldo Tavares, de 70 anos, mora desde os 8 anos no Alecrim — Foto: Victor Eduardo/Inter TV

🌿 De acordo com o historiador Henrique Lucena, o Alecrim foi formado no século 19, sendo povoado principalmente por uma população que fugia da seca para Natal. Lucena explicou que o nome dado à localidade ocorreu em referência ao Cemitério do Alecrim, que é mais antigo do que o próprio bairro.

"O nome do bairro advém do próprio cemitério, que é mais antigo do que o próprio bairro. Alecrim, aquela erva que a gente coloca na carne, ela também servia como uma forma de apaziguamento dos espíritos. E por causa disso, tinha -se a crença e a religiosidade de se plantar o alecrim sobre os túmulos", explicou.

O Alecrim também registrou, na década de 1940, a construção da Vila Naval, em um projeto ligado à expansão da Marinha do Brasil na capital.

Outro símbolo importante do bairro é a Praça Gentil Ferreira - também chamada de Praça do Relógio. Atualmente, a praça segue como ponto de encontro e ainda é palco de projetos como o Samba de Arruar.

As ruas do bairro também são bastante lembradas por terem, além dos nomes, uma referência de números (Avenida Dois, Avenida Dez...). O historiador contou que essa foi uma definição dada pelo segundo prefeito de Natal, Omar O'Grady.

A empresária Maria Luiza dos Santos chegou ao bairro com 14 anos, em 1994, e começou trabalhando na feira livre. Ela passou ainda pelo camelódromo até abrir a própria loja, uma ótica.

"Além de ser um bairro bastante movimentado, é um bairro central, muito conhecido e não só absorve pessoas da própria Natal, como de todo o Rio Grande do Norte", disse.

Para Maria Luiza, ser empreendedor "é um ato de fé". "Muitas vezes a empreendedora sai de casa e não marcou nada. Abre as portas e vem com aquela fé que vai aparecer o cliente", destacou.

Maria Luiza dos Santos trabalhou em várias funções no Alecrim — Foto: Victor Eduardo/Inter TV Cabugi

O amor pelo bairro, no entanto, não faz os comerciantes fecharem os olhos para os problemas. Eles reclamam de pontos como falta de segurança, desorganização e ausência de estacionamento para clientes.

"Deveria haver uma reorganização do bairro, ter possibilidade de estacionamento. Acho que isso realmente tira um pouco do comércio aqui. Eu tenho sentido que realmente houve uma queda no movimento, tanto de pessoas, como na próprio economia", falou a empresária Maria Luiza.

A comerciante Jani Rocha diz que o bairro precisa de atenção das autoridades para ficar "mais bonito e mais forte". Ela cita ainda falta de limpeza.

Comércio no bairro Alecrim, em Natal — Foto: Augusto César Gomes/g1

"Precisa muito de mais segurança, mais cuidado e mais conscientização das autoridades com as pessoas, para que mantenham a higiene, mantenham a limpeza. O cliente sente muito necessidade disso", falou.

"A gente por conta própria que sai limpando e não dá conta, porque o Alecrim é imenso", completou.

Para Maria Luiza Santos, apesar dos problemas, o Alecrim tem tradições que mantêm a clientela ativa no bairro.

"A feira livre já é tradição, e os próprios camelódromos. Esse comércio popular que tem aqui bem no meio da Avenida 2, também eu acredito que atrai bastante as pessoas", falou.

Além da praça, o bairro viu surgir nos seus limites geográficos o Alecrim Futebol Clube , terceiro maior campeão potiguar da história, com 7 títulos estaduais - atrás apenas de ABC e América.

O clube - também apelidado de Verdão ou Periquito - foi fundado em 15 de agosto de 1915 e recebeu esse nome em homenagem ao bairro onde estava localizado. "Um dos mais tradicionais também da cidade, todo com origem orientação identitária do bairro", falou o historiador Henrique Lucena.

Outro motivo de orgulho no bairro é o Teatro Sandoval Wanderley, conhecido como Teatrinho do Povo , que serviu como uma alternativa mais popular e destinada principalmente à classe trabalhadora na comparação com o Teatro Alberto Maranhão, que era tido como um teatro que servia apenas a elite nas décadas de 1960 e 1970.

Jani Rocha trabalha no Alecrim há mais de 25 anos — Foto: Victor Eduardo/Inter TV

articles.title: Grécia aprova proibição de redes sociais para menores de 15 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Medida entra em vigor em janeiro de 2027; plataformas terão dois meses e meio para criar uma forma de verificar a idade dos usuários e proteger sua privacidade.
articles.summary: Medida entra em vigor em janeiro de 2027; plataformas terão dois meses e meio para criar uma forma de verificar a idade dos usuários e proteger sua privacidade.
articles.body:
Criança mexendo no celular com as redes sociais visíveis no aparelho — Foto: Unsplash/Sanket Mishra

O Parlamento da Grécia aprovou nesta sexta-feira (23) um projeto de lei que proíbe o uso de redes sociais por menores de 15 anos.

A medida entra em vigor em 1º de janeiro de 2027 e ocorre em meio à crescente preocupação com os efeitos dessas plataformas sobre a saúde e a segurança de crianças e adolescentes.

O primeiro-ministro grego, Kyriakos Mitsotakis, afirmou que as plataformas terão dois meses e meio para desenvolver uma forma de verificar a idade dos usuários e proteger a privacidade deles .

A Grécia está entre os sete países da União Europeia que buscam uma solução para a verificação de idade em conjunto com a Comissão Europeia.

O governo grego afirma que a medida busca apoiar os pais no combate à "rolagem infinita" nas redes sociais, que tira das crianças horas de sono, concentração e tempo de convivência com os amigos.

Na França, uma lei semelhante foi derrubada pelo Conselho Constitucional em agosto. A previsão era que a medida começasse a valer em setembro.

Um dos principais problemas apontados pelo tribunal na França foi a necessidade de verificar a idade dos usuários . Segundo o Conselho Constitucional, ao impedir menores de 15 anos de acessar determinados serviços online, a lei faria com que todas as pessoas, inclusive adultos, precisassem comprovar a própria idade para utilizar essas plataformas.

articles.title: Prédio de mais de 10 andares desaba no Quênia; equipes buscam vítimas | G1
articles.standfirst: Operações de resgate buscam vítimas sob os escombros na região de Eastleigh. Autoridades alertam para risco de novo colapso.
articles.summary: Equipes de resgate buscam vítimas após prédio desaba em Nairóbi, no Quênia, em meio a alertas de novos colapsos e denúncias de irregularidades na obra.
articles.body:
Equipes de segurança e defesa civil trabalham após o desabamento de um prédio de vários andares em Nairóbi, Quênia — Foto: Brian Inganga/AP

Um prédio com mais de 10 andares desabou em Nairóbi, capital do Quênia, nesta sexta-feira (23), deixando uma enorme massa de concreto e mais de uma dúzia de andares sobrepostos. Ainda não há um balanço oficial do total de vítimas.

O prédio estava em construção em uma movimentada rua comercial na área de Eastleigh, em Nairóbi.

O chefe de polícia local, Issa Mohamud, afirmou que o prédio tinha mais de 10 andares superiores em construção.

A polícia precisou lançar gás lacrimogêneo contra pessoas que começaram a saquear lojas vizinhas, enquanto os agentes tentavam isolar a área e permitir o acesso das equipes de emergência.

Joseph Kaula conseguiu escapar por pouco. O estucador, que trabalhava no quinto andar, disse ter ouvido gritos e visto outros trabalhadores correndo para fora, gritando que o prédio estava desabando.

"Eu fui a última pessoa a sair antes do desabamento e toda a área ficou cheia de poeira", disse Kaula.

Kaula suspeita que alguns de seus colegas estejam presos no porão.

Uma mulher ferida foi resgatada e hospitalizada, e outra pessoa que gritava por socorro ficou em silêncio, disse o chefe de polícia.

Mohamud também alertou para a possibilidade de um segundo desabamento, já que o prédio que ruiu estava apoiado no prédio vizinho.

Equipes de segurança e defesa civil trabalham após o desabamento de um prédio de vários andares em Nairóbi — Foto: Brian Inganga/AP

Havia poucos equipamentos pesados disponíveis imediatamente. Horas depois, um grupo de socorristas com capacetes usava varas retiradas de árvores para cutucar a enorme pilha de entulho.

Uma escavadeira começou a remover o concreto aglomerado com aço. Depois, chegaram pelo menos mais duas pás carregadeiras.

Os socorristas esperavam conseguir acessar possíveis espaços intocados no porão e no térreo, que haviam sido alugados para uma loja de eletrônicos, um açougue e um mercado enquanto a construção continuava nos andares superiores.

Moradores relataram que alguns de seus entes queridos que ficaram presos fizeram ligações pedindo ajuda imediatamente após o desabamento, mas que seus telefones ficaram inacessíveis posteriormente.

Uma tenda foi montada para que as pessoas pudessem registrar os desaparecidos. Não se sabia quantas pessoas poderiam estar sob os escombros.

Os desabamentos de edifícios são um problema recorrente em Nairóbi. Os funcionários do condado responsáveis pela emissão de alvarás de construção têm sido acusados de não realizarem inspeções adequadas para garantir que os construtores cumpram as normas de segurança e os padrões de construção.

"Serão realizadas investigações", disse Mohamud. "Garantiremos que os responsáveis por qualquer negligência sejam responsabilizados perante a lei."

O governador de Nairóbi, Johnson Sakaja, afirmou que a construção do prédio havia sido aprovada, mas que este não possuía certificado de ocupação, o que tornava ilegal a abertura de lojas no térreo.

Ele defendeu que os governos dos condados do Quênia precisam de maior poder de fiscalização, argumentando que as atuais penalidades para o descumprimento das normas representam apenas uma "punição branda" para os construtores que violam os regulamentos.

Pessoas observam por trás de um cordão de segurança após o desabamento de um prédio de vários andares em Nairóbi, Quênia — Foto: Brian Inganga/AP

articles.title: Enem Filosofia: Professor explica a epistemologia de Platão | G1
articles.standfirst: Professor Ronaldo Oliveira detalha o dualismo platônico e a teoria da reminiscência para orientar estudantes na prova de Ciências Humanas do Enem.
articles.summary: O professor Ronaldo Oliveira detalha o dualismo platônico e a teoria da reminiscência para orientar estudantes na prova de Ciências Humanas do Enem.
articles.body:
O projeto Preparação, da TV Grande Rio e g1 Petrolina , traz nesta sexta-feira (23) uma dica de Filosofia para os estudantes que estão se preparando para o Enem . O exame será realizado nos dias 8 e 15 de novembro em todo o país.

O professor Ronaldo Oliveira dá dica sobre a epistemologia de Platão.

"A filosofia platônica é dualista, ou seja, para Platão, existe o mundo sensível e o mundo inteligível. Mundo sensível, mundo da caverna, da ignorância, do não conhecimento. Mundo dos sentidos, mundo inteligível, o mundo das formas perfeitas, eternas, imutáveis. O mundo do conhecimento universal. E, para Platão, como é que o indivíduo faz isso? Ele diz que o indivíduo deve fazer isso a partir do seu esforço intelectual. Para Platão, conhecer nada mais é do que recordar. É o que nós chamamos de reminiscência".

No vídeo acima , você confere a dica completa para ir muito bem na prova de Ciências Humanas e suas Tecnologias, Linguagens, Códigos e suas Tecnologias do Enem .

articles.title: ‘Not an error, it’s a crime’: UP CEO on 10,470 voter records altered after SIR final Roll in Pilibhit
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: “This is not an error or negligence. This is a crime.
articles.body: LUCKNOW: “This is not an error or negligence. This is a crime. It was done deliberately,” Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer (CEO) Navdeep Rinwa told TOI, as an FIR was registered against two electoral registration officers (EROs) and a computer operator for allegedly manipulating 10,470 voter records in Pilibhit after the final electoral roll was published on April 10 following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).The FIR, registered at Kotwali police station on October 22, names Mayank Goswami, then SDM Amaria and ERO; Hemant Kumar, then SDM and ERO; and Anil Kumar, computer assistant (VRC operator).They have been booked under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and Section 201 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.According to the FIR lodged by assistant district election officer Krishna Kumar Kashyap, 13,779 Form-8 applications were entered between May 31 and August 29, 2026, months after the April 10 SIR final roll.Of these, 10,470 were approved and 3,309 rejected.Of these, 4,717 entries were made until July 16, while another 9,062 were entered between July 17 and August 29. Significantly, no supporting application forms or documents for any of these entries were found in official records.All 10,470 approved entries were found irregular.Crucially, no supporting Form-8 applications or related records were found in the election office for any of the 13,779 entries.“There was no hacking, no system glitch and no technical malfunction. Those entrusted with maintaining the electoral rolls failed to discharge their responsibilities. The operator entered Form-8 applications without receiving them from voters, and the EROs approved them. This was a deliberate criminal act, not a clerical mistake,” Rinwa said.Explaining the authentication process, Rinwa said the operator enters Form-8 applications using his credentials, authenticated through an OTP sent to his registered mobile number.The ERO subsequently approves or rejects applications through a separate login, password and OTP authentication.“You cannot simply claim that somebody stole your password. An OTP also goes to your registered phone. Either you authenticate the transaction yourself or share the OTP with somebody. How can more than 10,000 such forms be approved without scrutiny? What were the EROs doing?” Rinwa questioned.He said Goswami was responsible for approvals between May 31 and July 16, while Hemant Kumar held responsibility from July 17 to August 29.Rinwa said Section 32 provides for imprisonment of up to two years, a fine, or both, for electoral officials guilty of acts or omissions without reasonable cause.“We have initiated the strictest possible legal action. The computer operator is being removed from service, while departmental disciplinary proceedings are being initiated against both SDMs, separately from the criminal proceedings before the court,” he said.The CEO said the investigation was being expanded beyond Form-8 corrections.“We have sought an examination of all Form-6 applications entered by this operator for inclusion of voters and all Form-7 applications for deletion of names. We have also ordered similar scrutiny in Pilibhit's remaining three assembly constituencies,” Rinwa said.“We have directed district magistrates across Uttar Pradesh to examine whether similar manipulation has occurred in their assembly constituencies and submit reports within two days,” he added, clarifying that reports were awaited as election officials had been occupied with polling duties.Advocate Faizan Ali Khan, among the first complainants, said he discovered the manipulation on October 12 when another person's name appeared against his EPIC number.“My name and my family members' details were correct in the April 10 final SIR list. When I compared subsequent electoral records, I found 142 altered voter entries among 1,037 voters at my polling booth,” Khan told TOI.“People had verified their names during SIR. articles.title: Psychology study explains why people struggle to give away their grandparents’ old belongings, even when they no longer use them
articles.summary: A cupboard full of unused crockery, an old grandfather’s watch or a stack of books inherited from a grandparent can take up space for years.
articles.body: A cupboard full of unused crockery, an old grandfather’s watch or a stack of books inherited from a grandparent can take up space for years. The items may no longer fit into everyday life, yet the thought of donating them can feel surprisingly difficult. Even when families are trying to declutter, some belongings remain untouched because giving them away feels like more than simply getting rid of old things.New research offers an explanation for this hesitation. Researchers found that people who inherit meaningful possessions often worry about what will happen to them after they leave the family. Their concern is not only about losing an object but also about whether the family history and legacy attached to it will continue.The study, titled “Preserving Legacy at Disposal: How Heritage Goods Shape Donation Allocation,” was co-authored by Hyewon Oh of the Stevens Institute of Technology and Ravi Mehta of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. Published in the 'Journal of the Association for Consumer Research', the research examined how people decide to give away possessions that carry a connection to their family’s past.Why an old possession can feel like part of the familyA dinner set inherited from a grandmother may have little practical value to someone who rarely hosts guests. But the same set could represent family celebrations, childhood memories and years of shared meals. This is what researchers describe as a heritage connection. An object becomes meaningful because it links its owner to a shared past, family traditions and people who came before them. When a possession carries that kind of meaning, deciding what to do with it becomes more complicated than assessing whether it is useful. Donating it can feel like losing a small, tangible connection to family history.The new study explored what happens when keeping these possessions is no longer practical. Across a qualitative pilot study and four experiments, the researchers found that heirs often preferred to donate meaningful items together rather than separate them among different recipients. The findings suggest that people may be willing to part with an object when they believe its story will continue in some form.Why people prefer to keep inherited sets togetherImagine inheriting a complete dinner set from a grandparent. Some plates could be donated to one charity, bowls to another and cups to a third. From a practical perspective, distributing the items this way might help more people. Yet heirs may prefer to donate the entire set to a single organisation. The researchers found that people often wanted to preserve what they described as the integrity of heritage goods. Keeping the items together helped maintain the sense that they belonged to a shared history rather than being a collection of unrelated objects.The same idea can apply to hardcover books, collections and other belongings passed down through generations. When the objects are seen as parts of a meaningful whole, splitting them up can feel like breaking apart the legacy they represent. However, the findings also revealed an important distinction. When people viewed items as independent objects rather than parts of a unified collection, they became more willing to distribute them among different charities if that increased the chances of the items being used. In other words, people may find it easier to let go when they believe the belongings will continue to serve a purpose.The emotional decision behind declutteringThe findings help explain why decluttering can become an emotional task, especially when families are downsizing or sorting through the belongings of ageing parents and relatives. A person may have no use for an inherited object but still feel responsible for deciding its future carefully. The hesitation does not necessarily mean they want to keep everything forever. They may simply be uncomfortable with the idea that something meaningful could be discarded, separated from its collection or passed on without its history being recognised.Earlier research published in the 'Journal of Marketing Research' also examined how people value heritage goods. In five studies, researchers Katherine L. Christensen and Suzanne B. Shu found that an object’s connection to shared history could influence how owners felt about passing it on. Concerns about losing that heritage connection helped explain their decisions. Together, the research suggests that the meaning attached to possessions can extend beyond personal memories. An inherited object may also represent continuity between generations, making the decision to part with it feel more significant than its practical value would suggest.How families can pass on heirlooms without losing their meaningThe findings could also help charities, resale platforms and organisations that encourage people to reuse unwanted possessions. Making donations easier may involve more than arranging collection or offering a convenient drop-off point. It may also mean recognising why the items matter to the people giving them away. For families, one practical approach is to consider whether a meaningful collection can be donated together. If that is not possible, they could look for recipients who will use the objects, rather than allowing them to remain boxed away indefinitely.Recording a short family story, identifying who an object belonged to or sharing photographs can also help preserve its history, even when the physical item moves to a new home. These are practical suggestions rather than interventions directly tested by the study, but they follow its central finding: people care about what happens to their family’s possessions after they let them go. Ultimately, an heirloom does not have to remain in the same cupboard to keep its meaning. For many people, the important question is whether the memories and history attached to it can continue beyond their own ownership. That may be why an old set of plates or a box of books can be so difficult to give away. People are not always holding on to the objects themselves. Sometimes, they are trying to find a way to let go without feeling that a piece of their family’s story is being lost.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Delhi HC rejects AISA chief Neha Bora's plea against police notice to sign peace bond
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court rejected a plea filed by All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora challenging a police notice directing
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court rejected a plea filed by All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora challenging a police notice directing her to execute a bond for “keeping peace” before a Special Executive Magistrate."I am rejecting the writ petition at this juncture," Justice Subramonium Prasad said while pronouncing the judgment.The judge, however, issued directions to the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) to provide the student leader with all relevant material related to the proceedings.Bora had moved the high court on Monday, arguing that the notice was vague, factually incorrect and unsupported by material establishing the likelihood of a breach of peace.She alleged that the proceedings were a “colourable exercise of preventive powers to suppress peaceful dissent, in violation of Articles 19(1)(a), 19(1)(b) and 21 of Constitution”.During Thursday's hearing, Bora's counsel argued that citizens do not need permission to hoist the national flag, referring to the police notice which alleged that she had hoisted the flag without valid permission.The notice, issued on October 17 under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directed Bora to appear before the magistrate on October 19 and explain why she should not execute a personal bond of Rs 10,000 with one surety “for keeping peace for a period of enquiry.”Bora was taken into preventive detention on October 16 while on her way to participate in the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march at Central Park in Connaught Place. She was released the following day.According to her petition, the police initiated proceedings based on alleged sloganeering at Mandi House on October 16, repeated protests around Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS, and allegations that she had instigated people to join a demonstration at Connaught Place on the same day.“The impugned notice rests on a prima facie incorrect fact, namely that the petitioner instigated people to participate in the demonstration at Central Park, CP on Oct 16. The petitioner’s call and the incident alleged were different. The petitioner called for a peaceful gathering at Mandi House at 5.00 pm on Oct 16, and it is a matter of record that she was detained from Mandi House,” Bora’s petition said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A Massachusetts couple cut trees from their own land to build barns for 20 rescued animals; horses saved from slaughter can live there without ever working again
articles.summary: In Norton, Massachusetts, Heidi and Bobby Medas have turned their own property into Smokey Chestnut Farm, a nonprofit sanctuary where rescued horses and
articles.body: In Norton, Massachusetts, Heidi and Bobby Medas have turned their own property into Smokey Chestnut Farm, a nonprofit sanctuary where rescued horses and other animals can live without being expected to work or entertain people. Using timber cut from their land, Bobby built barns to house the farm’s 20 residents, including horses saved from kill pens and the threat of slaughter. As reported by CBS News, what began as Heidi’s commitment to horse rescue has grown into a community effort supported by more than 60 volunteers. As the farm approaches its 15th anniversary in 2027, its mission extends beyond animal welfare, offering people a place to connect and contribute.How a couple turned their Massachusetts property into a refuge for rescued animalsHeidi and Bobby established Smokey Chestnut Farm as a nonprofit, with Bobby putting his practical skills to work on the land. A retired employee of Norton’s highway department, he built the barns and other structures using timber cut from the property itself. The farm now houses 20 rescued animals, including horses, mules, alpacas and pigs.The couple, who have been married for 42 years, did not set out to become public figures in their community. Heidi had been drawn to horse rescue, and the work gradually became a shared commitment. More than 60 volunteers now help support the operation, alongside thousands of people who contribute to its efforts.The farm is generally visited by appointment or during fundraising events. Its public profile grew during the Covid-19 pandemic, when people looked for outdoor activities and places to spend time away from crowded indoor settings. The couple also began giving away compost produced at the property, bringing more people into contact with the work being done there.Smokey Chestnut Farm is approaching its 15th anniversary in 2027. For Bobby, the attention and support have meant adjusting to a role he might not once have chosen.Rescued horses find lifelong sanctuary after facing the threat of slaughterSeveral of the farm’s horses were saved from kill pens, holding facilities where animals may be bought for onward transport to slaughterhouses, including those in Canada and Mexico. The costs of rescuing a horse extend beyond the purchase itself. Smokey Chestnut Farm must also cover transport and quarantine, with the final bill depending on the animal’s condition and the arrangements needed to bring it to safety.The scale of the wider problem is reflected in estimates from the US Department of Agriculture, which put the number of horses from the United States slaughtered each year at between 18,000 and 25,000. Horses continue to be consumed as meat in several parts of the world, although slaughter for human consumption is not carried out legally within the United States.At Smokey Chestnut Farm, the animals are not expected to work or provide entertainment. Most do not wear harnesses, and there is no requirement for them to be ridden or trained. The intention is to provide care for the remainder of their lives, regardless of whether they can be handled easily or have any practical use to people.From abuse to safety, rescued horses begin new lives at the farmHope and Faith, two Chincoteague ponies, remain wary of human contact. Heidi has described them as having been wild when they arrived, and they still prefer to keep their distance from people. They share their space with Lucky, a retired show pony whose former owners continue to visit. The older animal appears to have become a steady presence for the two ponies.Bonnie and Clyde, a pair of mules, were rescued from a kill pen in Pennsylvania. Clyde had suffered abuse before reaching the farm and initially spent much of his time standing in a corner, trembling. According to Heidi, his behaviour has improved since then. The pair live alongside Lucas, a large horse that was removed from an animal abuse case.Other residents have been surrendered for different reasons. Whiskey, a thoroughbred, was given up after failing to make money for his owner. Zilla, a Standardbred, had pulled a racing cart and worked with Amish families before being placed at risk of slaughter. Heidi received a call about Zilla and arranged for his rescue.When Zilla first arrived, he was frightened of people. Five years later, he had become comfortable in his surroundings. Heidi has described the change as a gradual process in which he came to recognise that he was safe.Rescuing blind horses became a personal commitmentTwo of the horses at the farm, Grace and Dakota, are blind. Dakota’s rescue began after Heidi received a video from a stranger showing the horse in a kill pen in Texas. She initially did not want to watch it, but her concern for the animal eventually led her to act.Dakota’s case also became part of a wider effort to save Kelsey, another blind horse who has since died. Heidi was determined to secure help for both animals, despite the practical and financial demands involved. Their stories reflect the farm’s policy of accepting animals on the basis of their need for care rather than their ability to be trained, ridden or used for work.The couple cannot take in every horse that needs rescuing. Smokey Chestnut Farm is currently full, meaning new arrivals must be accommodated elsewhere if they are to be saved. Fundraising therefore remains important even when the farm itself has no available space.Heidi has worked to build relationships with other rescuers so that a horse can still be helped when there is no room in Norton. One of those partnerships is with Annie Crosby, an animal rescuer based in Rehoboth, Massachusetts. The two have now rescued six horses together.Rescued animals bring companionship and a sense of purpose to volunteersThe sanctuary has also become an important place for people who spend time there. Crystal Medeiros, who volunteers at least four days a week, has found a particular connection with Zilla. Now retired, she has been able to pursue her longstanding wish to work with animals.Medeiros has spoken about the sense of peace she experiences at the farm and the relationships she has formed there. Caring for the animals gives her a routine built around practical tasks and attention to their needs. It also provides regular contact with people who share her interests.Annie Crosby, who also works as a therapist, has observed how time spent around horses can affect people. Her experience at the farm and through rescue work has shown her that the benefits are not confined to the animals themselves. The relationships formed around their care can matter to those involved, too.Heidi’s work with deaf students continues alongside the farmAnimal welfare is not Heidi’s only long-standing commitment. For more than 30 years, she has worked as an interpreter for deaf students at Boston University, transcribing lecture notes in real time so that students can follow their classes.She has spoken about the demands faced by students with disabilities and her admiration for those who continue to pursue their education despite the obstacles they encounter. The work has given her another way to provide practical support to people who need it.Her involvement in education and animal rescue may appear to be separate responsibilities, but both depend on close attention to others and an understanding that people and animals can need different kinds of assistance. At the farm, that means allowing a frightened horse to settle at its own pace. In the classroom, it means helping students access information as a lesson unfolds.You use AI every day. articles.title: Lauren Conrad’s ‘Laguna Beach’ family mansion, designed and built by her father James Conrad in 2004, listed for $26.5 million; inside the 8,000-square-foot oceanfront estate
articles.summary: Lauren Conrad’s family mansion, which featured in MTV’s hit reality show Laguna Beach: The Real Orange County, has hit the market for $26.5 million.
articles.body: Lauren Conrad’s family mansion, which featured in MTV’s hit reality show Laguna Beach: The Real Orange County, has hit the market for $26.5 million. The nearly 8,000-square-foot Mediterranean-style estate overlooks the Pacific Ocean from the exclusive Three Arch Bay community in Laguna Beach, California.According to Cottages & Gardens, the property was designed and built in 2004 by Conrad’s father, architect James Conrad. The home became familiar to fans through the early episodes of the reality series, which followed the lives, friendships and relationships of teenagers in Southern California. Richard Trey Dewey of Pacific Sotheby’s International Realty is handling the listing.Inside Lauren Conrad’s $26.5 million Laguna Beach mansionThe Mediterranean-style residence spans nearly 8,000 square feet and features six bedrooms, six full bathrooms and an additional half-bathroom. Its design combines Santa Barbara-inspired architecture with materials sourced from Italy, travertine flooring, arched windows and vaulted ceilings with exposed wooden beams.The home also includes formal living and dining rooms, two family rooms, a spacious eat-in kitchen with a large island and a private office. Wood-trimmed sliding glass doors, stone fireplaces and expansive terraces add to its traditional architectural appeal.According to the property listing, the rooms and outdoor spaces are positioned to take advantage of sweeping views of the Pacific Ocean and the Orange County coastline.Infinity-edge pool and private beach access add to the appealOne of the estate’s standout features is its infinity-edge swimming pool, which appears to merge with the ocean beyond. A large stone patio, towering palm trees and an expansive upper-level deck provide additional outdoor spaces for relaxation and entertaining.The property sits within Three Arch Bay, a guard-gated community known for its privacy and exclusive amenities. Ownership includes access to a private beach, clubhouse and tennis facilities.The combination of extensive land, ocean views, privacy and distinctive architecture is a major part of the appeal of the $26.5 million listing.Lauren Conrad’s family home featured in ‘Laguna Beach’Laguna Beach: The Real Orange County premiered on MTV in September 2004 and became one of the network’s defining reality shows of the mid-2000s. The series followed Conrad and her castmates through their teenage years, relationships and friendships in the affluent California coastal community.In the first episode, Conrad and castmate Stephen Colletti visit the family property while it is still under construction. The finished mansion later became part of the visual backdrop associated with the show.The series ran for three seasons, concluding in 2006. Its popularity helped launch the careers of several cast members, including Conrad and Kristin Cavallari, whose rivalry became one of the show's most talked-about storylines.In March 2026, Conrad and Cavallari reunited with other cast members for a 20th-anniversary special, bringing renewed attention to the series and its legacy.Lauren Conrad’s real estate moves over the yearsConrad has made several high-value real estate moves since her reality television days. In 2017, around the time she was expecting her first child, she listed a Pacific Palisades home for $5.2 million and a Brentwood estate for $4.5 million. Both properties reportedly sold at a profit.Conrad and her family have also maintained ties to Laguna Beach. In 2014, the Los Angeles Times reported that she had purchased an oceanfront home in the area for $8.5 million. The property was located in the Three Arch Bay community and offered views of the coastline.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: ‘Like being raped all over again’: UK detective assaulted by coworker questions probe
articles.summary: A Metropolitan Police detective who was raped by former Scotland Yard officer David Carrick has called for commissioner Sir Mark Rowley to resign, saying
articles.body: A Metropolitan Police detective who was raped by former Scotland Yard officer David Carrick has called for commissioner Sir Mark Rowley to resign, saying the force’s handling of her subsequent legal battle was “like being raped all over again”.Detective Constable Linda Williams, 60, was attacked by Carrick in 2004. She later brought a civil claim against the Metropolitan Police for failing to protect her from the serial sex offender. The case has now been settled for an undisclosed six-figure sum, with the force paying compensation without admitting liability, The Guardian reported.Williams told the BBC that the lengthy legal proceedings had been “horrific” and left her contemplating suicide. She said the “worst thing” was that lawyers representing the Met challenged the severity of her post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), arguing that she had been raped only once.“They used the fact that I just got on with my life as best I could after the rape against me,” she said, adding that her ability to continue performing well at work was cited as evidence that she had shown no signs of psychological trauma.Carrick, who served as an armed officer in the Met, was jailed in 2023 after admitting to 71 sexual offences, including 48 rapes involving 12 women. He is serving 37 life sentences. He was later convicted of further offences involving a child and a former partner.Williams reported the rape in 2021 after seeing media coverage of Carrick being charged with attacking another woman. Hertfordshire Police investigated the case and brought him to justice.In an unprecedented move for a serving officer, Williams has publicly demanded Rowley’s resignation, saying she believes little has changed in the force’s culture and that she no longer trusts the police to handle sexual violence cases appropriately.“If I was raped tomorrow, I wouldn’t report it,” she told The Guardian, citing what she described as a complete lack of empathy and support from the police.Rowley took charge of the Met in 2022, pledging to reform the force following a series of scandals, including the murder of Sarah Everard by a serving officer. A report by Baroness Casey in 2023 described the force as institutionally misogynistic.A Met spokesperson said serious flaws in the force’s handling of investigations had meant officers failed to identify Carrick’s pattern of abusive behaviour. The force said it regretted the failures and had sought to handle Williams’ claim as quickly and compassionately as possible.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2019, Alicia Keys and Swizz Beatz paid $20.8 million for a glass-walled California cliff house that had originally been offered for $30 million; two years later, they revealed its transformation into an art-filled family retreat
articles.summary: Musician Alicia Keys and her husband, record producer Swizz Beatz, bought one of Southern California's best-known architectural homes for $20.8 million
articles.body: Musician Alicia Keys and her husband, record producer Swizz Beatz, bought one of Southern California's best-known architectural homes for $20.8 million (£16 million) in 2019. They paid nearly $10 million less than the original asking price before turning the oceanfront property into an art-filled family home. Known as the Razor House, the glass-and-concrete estate sits on a cliff in La Jolla, near San Diego, overlooking the Pacific Ocean. According to Architectural Digest, the 11,000-square-foot property was first listed for $30 million. The couple completed the purchase in late 2019. Two years later, the couple opened the doors of their cliffside home to show how they had turned the unusual building, which extends out over the landscape, into a peaceful retreat filled with art for themselves and their children.Engineering on the La Jolla cliffsDesigned by well-known architect Wallace E. Cunningham and completed in 2007, the Razor House takes its name from the sharp-edged coastal cliff where it stands. The building features sweeping curves, floor-to-ceiling glass walls and solid concrete beams that extend outward over the ocean.According to architectural records cited by Architectural Digest, building the home required major engineering work to secure its heavy concrete frame to the coastal bedrock. The house covers several levels linked by a glass elevator. Its design gives almost every room clear, uninterrupted views of the sea. The property has six bedrooms, a main living pavilion, an underground garage that can hold up to eight vehicles, a private cinema and a guest house. Outside, an infinity-edge swimming pool creates the impression that it drops straight into the ocean below.Curating an extensive art collectionAfter Keys and Swizz Beatz, whose real name is Kasseem Dean, took ownership of the home, they worked with interior designer Kelly Behun to bring warmth and personal touches to its modern concrete spaces. The couple used the large walls and open gallery spaces to display important works from the Dean Collection. Their private art collection includes contemporary pieces by Black artists and creators from around the world. In a feature published by Architectural Digest in late 2021, Keys explained how the home's unusual shape and design influenced their choices of furniture and artwork. "When you choose a house like this, you have to respect its architecture," Keys told Architectural Digest during the home tour. "We wanted to make sure it felt like a home, not just a museum." The interiors now feature major works by Kehinde Wiley, Lynette Yiadom-Boakye, Gordon Parks and Nick Cave. The couple chose low-profile furniture covered in soft, textured materials such as velvet, wool and shearling. These pieces soften the exposed concrete surfaces without blocking the coastal views.A long-cherished dream realizedSwizz Beatz revealed that he had used a picture of the Razor House as his phone's screensaver for eight years before buying it. He had admired Cunningham's architecture long before the property came up for sale. When the estate went into foreclosure and appeared on the market at a lower price in 2019, the couple moved quickly to buy it. "It's a place where you can sit and contemplate, write, and create," Swizz Beatz told Architectural Digest in the 2021 interview. He described the home as both a place for creative work and a comfortable family retreat. "It was meant to be our place of peace." The main living room, which the family calls the "Dreamland" room, features a custom piano. Keys regularly uses it to compose music while looking out over the Pacific coastline.Living in a modern architectural iconBeyond serving as a private home, the Razor House has become a well-known part of popular culture. Its futuristic design and dramatic cliffside position have led many local residents and architecture fans to compare it to the fictional Malibu mansion of Marvel character Tony Stark. The estate also has large outdoor terraces, a rooftop entertainment deck with an outdoor kitchen and private paths leading towards the beach below. Custom lighting built into the concrete structure lights up the home after dark without creating glare on its floor-to-ceiling glass walls. Property records confirm that the $20.8 million sale ranks among the highest property sales ever recorded in La Jolla. The price reflects both the lasting value of Cunningham's architectural design and the continued appeal of coastal California real estate.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Rhode Island collected more than 600 unwanted Christmas trees in 2026, but instead of sending them to landfills, volunteers are placing them along damaged streams to rebuild riverbanks and shelter young trout
articles.summary: Volunteers across Rhode Island have collected more than 600 discarded Christmas trees in 2026 to help repair damaged riverbanks and protect wild trout.
articles.body: Volunteers across Rhode Island have collected more than 600 discarded Christmas trees in 2026 to help repair damaged riverbanks and protect wild trout. The effort turns holiday waste into valuable underwater habitat for fish and other aquatic life. The statewide project, known as "Trees for Trout," is a joint effort by the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management (DEM) Division of Fish and Wildlife and the Rhode Island chapter of Trout Unlimited. Instead of sending used Christmas trees to landfills, residents brought hundreds of real evergreen trees to collection events at the Arcadia Management Area in Exeter. According to event details published by the Department of Environmental Management, the trees will be reused to improve local waterways. The collected trees are being secured along damaged streams throughout the Wood River watershed. The aim is to reduce soil erosion caused by extreme weather and severe flooding.Building conifer revetments along damaged streamsRiverbank erosion has become worse along several Rhode Island waterways after powerful storms and heavy flooding. As a result, some river channels have become wider and shallower, making the water more likely to heat up. To help repair this damage, volunteers place and secure evergreen trees along eroded riverbanks. These natural barriers are known as conifer revetments. According to guidelines published by the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management, the submerged trees slow the water flowing near the riverbank. As water passes through the thick evergreen branches, heavier soil particles settle out of the moving water and collect around the base of the trees. Over time, the pine needles and wood slowly break down, while the trapped soil builds up and helps rebuild a stable riverbank. This process also makes the river channel narrower, allowing the main current to flow through a deeper, cooler section.Shelter for young trout and aquatic lifeDeep, cool water is vital for wild brook trout, a native fish species that cannot easily tolerate rising water temperatures. The network of underwater branches quickly provides shelter for young fish. Juvenile trout, small aquatic insects known as macroinvertebrates, and other small water creatures use the submerged pine branches as hiding places. These natural shelters help them escape larger fish and birds that hunt them. Event information published by Trout Unlimited states that volunteers meet at the Arcadia Check Station on Ten Rod Road in Exeter before travelling to selected stream locations. Wearing waders and heavy gloves and carrying hand tools, team members secure each tree to the stream bed. They use biodegradable stakes or natural cable anchors to stop high spring waters from carrying the trees downstream. The organisation requires all donated trees to be free of artificial tinsel, metal ornaments, lighting wires and chemical fire retardants. These materials could pollute freshwater habitats and harm aquatic life.Community participation and long-term impactThe "Trees for Trout" program depends entirely on community support. Local families, environmental groups and recreational anglers take part in winter tree collection drives and summer installation events. According to the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management, reusing Christmas trees for stream restoration provides two main benefits. It keeps hundreds of large organic items out of municipal waste systems and supplies low-cost materials for environmental restoration work. Freshwater fishing generates millions of dollars in economic activity each year across Rhode Island. Financial reports from the DEM Division of Fish and Wildlife link this activity to federal restoration grants and local fishing license sales. Projects such as conifer revetments help protect wild fish populations that reproduce naturally, allowing them to survive alongside fish raised and released through stocking programs. Volunteers will continue placing the remaining collected trees along priority streams throughout the warmer months. The work will give damaged riverbanks time to rebuild naturally before winter weather returns.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Remove service road first, then build flyover, delegation tells NHAI
articles.summary: Kolhapur: Activists urge NHAI to remove the raised service road before building the Panchganga flyover, citing flood risks; collector promises design changes first.
articles.body: Kolhapur: As part of the ongoing widening of Pune-Bengaluru National Highway, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) plans to construct a strategic bridge over Panchganga river between Pulachi Shiroli and Ujlaiwadi villages, adjacent to Kolhapur city. The project is specifically aimed at preventing severe monsoon flooding on this crucial stretch of the highway.However, the project has run into local opposition. Members of Mahapur Sangharsh Samiti have expressed concern that the existing service road, which sits higher than the main highway, could act as a barrier, obstructing the natural flow of floodwater and worsening accumulation in nearby areas.A delegation from the samiti met with district collector Dr Vijay Rathod and senior NHAI officials, demanding the complete removal of existing service road before work on the proposed flyover begins. The activists alleged that the current bridge design contains critical flaws and warned that proceeding without rectifying them could trigger catastrophic flooding during future monsoons.Responding to these apprehensions, district collector Dr. Vijay Rathod assured the delegation that construction would only commence after the necessary design modifications are made to ensure public safety.Girish Phonde, coordinator of Mahapur Sangharsh Samiti, stated that the bridge proposed on Sangli Phata–Ujlaiwadi route initially featured structural elements that risked creating a dam-like obstruction. Such a barrier, he argued, would inevitably force floodwaters into Kolhapur city and neighbouring villages.“Following opposition from the local gram panchayat, the design was modified to a bridge supported by pillars. However, we recently noticed that the service road leading to the bridge is being filled up, effectively creating a massive mud wall. The design presented by the NHAI still has fundamental flaws. Infrastructure projects of this scale must be designed keeping the environmental realities of the next 50 years in mind,” Phonde said.Environmental expert Uday Gaikwad also flagged vulnerabilities in the current blueprint. He emphasised that the state irrigation department should only grant a no-objection certificate (NOC) after thoroughly reviewing the record-breaking flood levels witnessed during the 2019 and 2021 monsoons.Warning of direct action, the activists said they would physically halt the highway construction if NHAI fails to implement the required design corrections immediately.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolhapur | Silver Rate in Kolhapur | Bank Holidays in Kolhapur | Public Holidays in KolhapurStay updated with the latest Kolhapur news. articles.title: Chaos in Punjab House as Cong walks out; Khaira suspended for session
articles.summary: Punjab assembly saw chaos as Congress demanded CM Bhagwant Mann’s resignation and walked out; MLA Sukhpal Khaira suspended for session over remarks.
articles.body: Chandigarh: The Punjab assembly witnessed chaotic scenes on Friday as Congress MLAs demanded chief minister Bhagwant Mann’s resignation, stormed the well of the House and staged a walkout. In response, the House moved and unanimously passed a motion suspending Congress MLA Sukhpal Singh Khaira for the remainder of the session for allegedly using objectionable language against the Chair.Wearing black scarves, Congress members arrived intent on cornering the governing party. They produced a flex-printed ‘Laanat Patra’ (letter of condemnation), accusing the govt of mishandling sacrilege cases, patronising drug and mining mafias, shielding gangsters, weakening farmers’ movement and failing to protect agricultural incomes amid rising state debt.Trouble began during Question Hour when leader of opposition Partap Singh Bajwa demanded Mann’s resignation. Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan asked members to reserve their issues for Zero Hour, but Congress legislators entered the well and exchanged slogans with AAP members.Appealing to the opposition, Sandhwan said the questions listed for the session concerned problems faced by the people of Punjab and urged senior Congress MLAs to set an example for first-time legislators.Amid the din, finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema clashed with Khaira and launched a scathing attack on the Congress, accusing the party of introducing “chitta”, a term commonly used for heroin. The minister also accused the Congress of taking false oaths on the Gutka Sahib, misleading people and doing politics over bodies. Congress MLAs subsequently walked out, with some tearing up and throwing papers towards the Chair.Cheema then moved a resolution to suspend Khaira, alleging that he had used derogatory language that insulted labourers, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. The motion was passed unanimously by the members present. He also urged the House to pass a separate resolution condemning the Congress over the alleged remarks.Reacting to his suspension on social media, Khaira said he would continue to raise issues concerning Punjab, slain anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota and the death of Dalit labourer Gulzar Dirba. articles.title: Kolkata Couple’s Pandal-Hopping Reel On ‘Real Happiness’ Wins Hearts Online
articles.summary: Viral Kolkata pandal-hopping reel shows a couple and son on a rickshaw, sparking online talk on “real happiness”; CESC’s Sanjiv Goenka praises the family.
articles.body: Kolkata: What defines success in life? A 20-second selfie video—capturing a simple pandal-hopping moment from a middle-aged couple’s life—that has gone viral on the internet apparently holds the answer, opine netizens.The video, which is winning hearts on the internet, shows the couple and their son smiling into a phone camera as they ride through the streets in the city on a hand-pulled rickshaw with lights dazzling in the backdrop.The video, featuring Abhishek Mukherjee, an employee of CESC Ltd, and his family has even drawn praise from his employer, Sanjiv Goenka, the chairman of RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group.Their spontaneous smiles and cheerful singalong have struck a chord with viewers, prompting conversations about happiness, family and the tendency to equate success with material wealth. Educator Amit Kilhor shared the video on X on Thursday, describing it as an example of what winning at life looks like.Calling it “Exemplar A” of how to define success, Kilhor wrote that it “should collectively be declared as the best video on Twitter for 2026”. Goenka identified Mukherjee as an employee of the group’s flagship power utility. “Some moments have a way of bringing a smile to everyone’s face,” Goenka wrote. He added, “It is heartening to see RPSGian Abhishek Mukherjee from @CESCLimited and his family capturing the joy of Pujo so naturally and winning hearts along the way.”TOI spoke to senior officials of CESC to connect with Mukherjee but he couldn’t be connected till late on Thursday. The video also triggered a wider conversation about wealth and contentment. The account peek_humour joked that Elon Musk “is still the second richest guy in the world”, suggesting that happiness cannot be measured by a bank balance.User Ritika viewed the clip as an illustration of Bengali men sharing household responsibilities and appreciating their wives’ efforts, sparking a debate about gender roles.Another user, Mishhteeee, cautioned against interpreting the family’s rickshaw ride as a sign of poverty. Pointing to Durga Puja traffic restrictions, she said a rickshaw was a practical way to get around and urged people to stop “overanalysis” of what she called “pure, wholesome family joy”.Amid Kolkata’s elaborate pandals and spectacular illuminations, the family’s simple outing offered a reminder that the festival’s happiest moments need neither grandeur nor extravagance — just the joy of being together.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: Meghalya CM addresses SPARK summit in Tura
articles.summary: Meghalaya CM Conrad K Sangma addresses SPARK State Summit ’26 in Tura, urging youth to embrace diversity, build confidence and values.
articles.body: Shillong: Students from across Meghalaya attended the SPARK Meghalaya State Summit ’26 in Tura on Friday.The School Programmes for Articulation, Resilience and Kindness (SPARK) summit was organised by the state education department and attended by CM Conrad K Sangma as chief guest.Addressing the students, Sangma recalled last year’s summit in Shillong and said he had suggested holding this year’s event in Tura.“The reason is that youngsters need to share and experience the true richness of the state – its diversity, cultures, language, land, beauty, food and music. The journey and stay are part of the experience they will carry forever,” Sangma said.“The summit is giving an opportunity for youth to interact, meet and understand different cultures and flavours of the people,” he said.He told the participants that the programme aimed to build confidence, instil values, foster friendships and help create better human beings.“This programme is at the heart of promoting talent and giving confidence to say ‘I will try’,” he said.Sangma called the youth the “greatest strength” of the state and said govt must channel their energy productively.He cited the Meghalaya Grassroots Music Project, saying 8,000 artists were earning through more than 20,000 performances with govt support, including shows in Japan and Germany.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news.
